title: Wendell and the Cipher
premise: Wendell Delacroix, a night dispatcher who has spent three years cataloguing the secrets of Grayhaven's callers, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after a fisherman's funeral—a letter naming Wendell himself as the only person who can find the witness everyone insists drowned years ago. Following the letter's cipher through taxi logs and tide charts, Wendell discovers the 'dead' witness is alive, hidden by the same people who buried the original crime. When the tide finally gives up what it took, Wendell must choose between exposing the town's complicity and protecting the fragile belonging he has finally found.
about_author: Oscar Blackwood is the pen name of a former harbor-town radio operator who spent a decade listening to strangers confess between midnight and dawn. He writes mysteries about quiet people who know too much.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Third-person limited from Wendell's POV: a routine night shift establishes his filing system of overheard confessions and his deliberate invisibility in Grayhaven. The emotional beat is loneliness disguised as control—until the last call of the night ends in silence.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV: among funeral condolences for fisherman Elias Marsh arrives a confession letter describing a drowning that never happened—and naming Wendell as its intended reader. The beat is dread; the cipher inside uses taxi dispatch codes only he would recognize.

chapters.title: Dead Air on Channel Four
chapters.summary: Wendell traces the dispatch codes to calls logged three years ago, discovering someone used his own system to hide a message. A threatening phone call warns him to stop. Beat: paranoia—the invisible man realizes he was never unseen.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Deputy Corinne Voss, who suspects Wendell knows more than he says about Elias's death. Their wary alliance forms over evidence the tide returned: a shoe belonging to a woman declared dead in 2019. Beat: reluctant trust.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Wendell decodes the full cipher: the witness, Mara Quist, faked her death with Elias's help and has been hiding in plain sight. But the letter's author isn't Mara—it's her protector, now silenced. Beat: revelation shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Corinne's POV: pressure descends from the town council to close the case as accidental drowning. Wendell realizes the conspiracy includes people who have been kind to him. Beat: betrayal—the belonging he craved was built on the crime.

chapters.title: Dispatch at Low Water
chapters.summary: Wendell uses the taxi company itself—fake bookings, coded routes—to move undetected toward Mara's hiding place while being followed. A near-fatal confrontation in the marsh. Beat: courage; the invisible man steps into the open.

chapters.title: The Confession Letter, Continued
chapters.summary: Mara's POV: she reveals why she stayed silent—her testimony would implicate her own brother—and why she chose Wendell, the one man who files secrets instead of spending them. Beat: empathy across guilt; two keepers of other people's sins.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Climax: at spring tide, the conspirators attempt to destroy the final evidence, and Wendell broadcasts the truth the only way he can—over the dispatch channel, letting the whole town hear the confession read aloud. Beat: exposure, danger, and moral choice.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Filing System
chapters.summary: Resolution: justice comes sideways—through Corinne's investigation and the town's own shame—while Wendell burns his alphabetized archive of secrets and keeps only one letter. Mara stays; Wendell, finally visible, belongs. Beat: quiet redemption.
